stem: Let a, b, and c be three non-zero vectors such that no two of these are collinear. If the vector a+2b is collinear with c and b+3c is collinear with a, then a+2b+6c equals
solution: Since \(\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}\) is collinear with \(\vec{c}\), write \(\vec{a} + 2\vec{b} = \lambda\vec{c}\). Since \(\vec{b} + 3\vec{c}\) is collinear with \(\vec{a}\), write \(\vec{b} + 3\vec{c} = \mu\vec{a}\), i.e. \(\vec{b} = \mu\vec{a} - 3\vec{c}\). Substituting into the first relation: \(\vec{a} + 2(\mu\vec{a} - 3\vec{c}) = \lambda\vec{c} \Rightarrow (1 + 2\mu)\vec{a} = (\lambda + 6)\vec{c}\). Because \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{c}\) are non-zero and non-collinear, both coefficients must vanish: \(1 + 2\mu = 0\) and \(\lambda + 6 = 0\), so \(\lambda = -6\). Therefore \(\vec{a} + 2\vec{b} + 6\vec{c} = \lambda\vec{c} + 6\vec{c} = -6\vec{c} + 6\vec{c} = \vec{0}\). Hence (D).
